targets.authors: Chan, J. Y. C., & Mazzocco, M. M.
targets.title: Competing features influence children’s attention to number.
targets.evidence_quote: First, we aimed to replicate our original findings (Chan & Mazzocco, 2017) with a different sample of preschoolers and adults, using the AtN task.
targets.outcome_quote: The results for number-based matches partially held when the total match score was used as the dependent variable (Figure 2b). Consistent with the best match score analyses, the significant main effect of Salience held, F(1, 89) = 10.16, p = .002, !! " = .102, with adults selecting number-based matches more frequently when alternative choices were of low salience (M = 4.16, SD = 3.00) compared to high salience (M = 3.38, SD = 3.29). The significant main effect of Order also held, F(1, 89) = 5.08, p = .027, !! " = .054, with adults making number- based matches more frequently when low salience trials came first (M = 4.49, SD = 3.17) compared to when high salience trials came first (M = 3.14, SD = 3.04). However, unlike this sample’s best match score or the total match scores we reported earlier (Chan & Mazzocco, 2017), there was no significant Salience × Order interaction on total match scores, p = .567, !! " = .004.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Both studies confirm the main salience finding, but authors explicitly contrast current results with the original: the adult total-match Salience × Order interaction did not recur, and other order-effect comparisons differ. Statements confirming main effects are individual comparisons rather than an overall verdict overriding these explicit contrasts.
